title: Localization of the proper integral scalar square
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, prime, algebraic closure and separated finite-type proper morphism of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let D be the normalized integral direct images, R their raw rational comparisons satisfying HasComparisonLaws [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison], S the normalized compact coefficient action [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action], and theta integral identity-compactification isomorphisms. Assume the integral scalar square of [lem-weil-proper-integral-scalar-square]. Let r_E be rational isomorphisms whose forward components are the localizations of theta_E. Let beta be natural isomorphisms R.rational_E followed by the target stage transition to the source stage transition followed by R.rational_L, whose components are the inverses of R.theta, using the actual stage systems [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Then at every E <= L and K the transition of r_E followed by beta equals S.beta followed by r_L at the transitioned K. Equality is heterogeneous only to transport the equal endpoint functors. Prerequisites: [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison], [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [lem-weil-proper-integral-scalar-square], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-proper-coefficient-descent-data].

proof.text: Identify the transitions of the chosen stage system with the raw rational scalar transitions. Their object and pure-tensor formulas identify the transition of the localization of an integral arrow with the localization of its integral transition: the coefficient map sends one to one.

Use the component formulas of r, the compact rationalBeta and the ordinary HasComparisonLaws to identify all four arrows in the square with integral localizations. The inverse ordinary comparison is identified by uniqueness of inverse after the endpoint equalities. Apply the target localization functor to the integral square and use preservation of composition. Compose the resulting heterogeneous equalities.

lean.statement: theorem rationalScalarSquare (D : SfStrictDirectImageScalar.IntegralComparisons l Ω f) (R : SfStrictDirectImageScalar.Comparisons l Ω f D) (hR : SfStrictDirectImageScalar.HasComparisonLaws l Ω f D R) (S : SfCompactSupportCoefficientAction l B.k (PurCompactSupport.coefficientPrimeUnit l B hl) Ω (Compactification.ofIsProper f)) (θ : ∀ E : Index l Ω, compactIntegral l Ω B hl f E ≅ (D.integral E).image) (hI : ∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) X), (integralTransition l Ω Y E L h).map ((θ E).hom.app K) ≫ (D.integralComparison E L h).inv.app K = (S.integralBeta h).hom.app K ≫ (θ L).hom.app ((integralTransition l Ω X E L h).obj K)) (r : ∀ E : Index l Ω, S.system.Φ E ≅ R.rational E) (hr : ∀ (E : Index l Ω) (K : Stage l Ω X E), HEq ((r E).hom.app K) ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) Y).map ((θ E).hom.app K.obj))) (β : ∀ {E L : Index l Ω} (h : E ≤ L), R.rational E ⋙ stageTransition l Ω Y E L h ≅ stageTransition l Ω X E L h ⋙ R.rational L) (hβ : ∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (K : Stage l Ω X E), HEq ((β h).hom.app K) ((R.theta E L h).inv.app K)) : ∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (K : Stage l Ω X E), HEq ((stageTransition l Ω Y E L h).map ((r E).hom.app K) ≫ (β h).hom.app K) ((S.system.β h).hom.app K ≫ (r L).hom.app ((stageTransition l Ω X E L h).obj K))
